markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting point.** (1) SASRec can represent both recent and distant interactions, but attention alone does not guarantee current-purpose specificity. The user diagnosis identifies stale interests competing with recent themes. (2) Broad associations dilute immediately relevant recommendations. A recent-context branch could emphasize repeated local preferences, although histories cannot establish compatibility or purchase purpose. (3) Electronics has 14.95% sampled wrong ranks and a −0.4812 margin tenth percentile. These motivate representation experiments; embedding similarity near 0.54–0.56 does not establish severe collapse.

**Related work.** (1) LSIDN separates persistent and immediate interests; TLSTSRec adaptively fuses temporal representations. Their connection motivates a minimal recent/full-history gate. (2) gSASRec combines multiple negatives with calibrated BCE. It motivates an objective ablation without establishing gains here. (3) TGCL4SR incorporates global transitions alongside sequences. Training-only directional associations could complement preference similarity, but cannot certify complementarity.

### Framework and candidate assessment

The framework separates **context selection** (recent/full history), **ranking supervision** (negative sampling), and **association evidence** (directed transitions). Test each axis separately before combining them.

Scores are 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell gives a positive and a limitation. User/model alignment describes hypotheses, not measured improvements.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Gated recent/full SASRec | 3: targeted adaptation; established fusion | 7: reusable context control; may overfit | 8: targets stale interests and broad matches; cannot verify purpose | 6: could resolve confused representations; margins may persist | 3: small branch; causal masking needs care |
| B. 32-negative calibrated BCE | 2: established objective; little novelty | 7: stronger comparisons; added cost | 4: may sharpen ranking; no explicit intent mechanism | 8: targets weak separation; sampled margins differ from HR | 4: vectorizable; calibration requires testing |
| C. Directed-transition late fusion | 3: useful adaptation; familiar graph signal | 6: captures order; sparse transitions | 6: supports next-action associations; cannot identify redundancy | 6: complementary scores; noisy counts | 4: sparse implementation; score normalization needed |

### Selected idea: gated recent/full SASRec

At 0% progress, select **A** for feasibility. It explicitly targets **historical-interest persistence** and **broad associations outranking specific recent matches**. Its model-facing target is weak positive–negative separation, especially Electronics; improvement remains unverified.

At each causal position, combine the SASRec state with a projected mean of the last five nonpadding item embeddings. A scalar sigmoid gate observes both representations and available window length. Initialize its recent contribution near 0.1 and retain baseline BCE to isolate context selection.

```text
h = SASRec(prefix)
r = project(mean(last_5_valid_embeddings(prefix)))
g = sigmoid(gate(concat(h, r, window_length)))
z = LayerNorm((1-g)*h + g*r)
score(item) = dot(z, item_embedding[item])
```

Train all four routed models with unchanged splits and seeds. Select baseline versus gated checkpoints using pinned macro validation HR@10; report category results and GPU cost. Update predictor generation and diagnostic scoring consistently. Preserve diagnostic interfaces, measure margins, and omit unavailable category attribution. Use no review attributes, pretrained weights, or hidden test data.

idea.description: Add a small adaptive gate between SASRec's causal sequence representation and a projected mean of the five most recent valid item embeddings.
idea.motivation: The branch explicitly addresses stale historical interests and broadly related recommendations displacing specific recent matches. It also tests whether context selection improves the weak sampled positive–negative separation observed most strongly in Electronics.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain baseline BCE, shared item embeddings, dataset routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Compute recent windows causally at every training position, excluding padding and future targets. Normalize window length before providing it to the gate; initialize the gate bias so its recent contribution is approximately 0.1. Handle empty windows with zeros and mask their losses. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; save checkpoints and generated working/predict.py beneath the trial directory. The predictor writer must instantiate and load the gate, projection, and normalization parameters. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Ensure log2feats and predict_score expose the actual fused representation and scoring rule. Return measured metrics and definitions, marking unavailable metadata attribution as unavailable. Select exclusively using the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; record per-category results and GPU cost within the shared budget. This proposal has not been trained or evaluated.
idea.pseudocode:
h = sasrec.log2feats(sequence)
r, count = causal_recent_mean(item_emb(sequence), window=5, exclude_padding=True)
r = recent_projection(r)
g = sigmoid(gate(concat(h, r, count / 5)))
z = layer_norm((1 - g) * h + g * r)
pos_logits = dot(z, item_emb(positive))
neg_logits = dot(z, item_emb(negative))
loss = masked_baseline_bce(pos_logits, neg_logits, positive != 0)
# Inference and diagnosis use the same fused z and shared item scoring.

originality.positive: A minimal, diagnosis-driven adaptation makes recent-context influence explicit.
originality.negative: Adaptive fusion of short- and long-term representations is well established.

future_potential.positive: Provides a simple foundation for later timestamp conditioning and context-specific ranking experiments.
future_potential.negative: A short window may amplify incidental purchases, and validation gains are unverified.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires only a causal pooling operation, projection, scalar gate, and matching inference changes.
code_difficulty.negative: Padding, causal windows, checkpoint compatibility, and diagnostic representation consistency require care.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Uses causal self-attention to encode interaction histories for next-item recommendation.
limitations: Does not explicitly separate recent intent from persistent preference.

related_work.title: LSIDN
contributions: Separates long- and short-term interests using distinct encoders and denoising strategies.
limitations: The supplied evidence does not establish improvements under this pinned RecHarness protocol.

related_work.title: TLSTSRec
contributions: Models temporal duration and spectrum and adaptively fuses long- and short-term representations.
limitations: Its temporal architecture is more involved than the proposed initial gate experiment.

related_work.title: gSASRec — IJCAI 2024 extended abstract
contributions: Combines multiple negatives with generalized BCE to address sampling-induced overconfidence.
limitations: Additional negatives increase computation and memory; gains on these four datasets remain unverified.

related_work.title: TGCL4SR
contributions: Combines global temporal transition graphs with local sequence encoding.
limitations: Does not establish that simple transition-score fusion improves the supplied baseline or identifies true complementarity.
